title: System Ownership
hook: One algorithm change and half your sales disappear. That's not a business you control.
statement: Real control comes from owning the things you can't afford to lose access to.
explainer: Platforms, one big client, a landlord. When someone else holds the key, they set the terms. Owning your list, your space, and your client base keeps you free.
sop: List your top 5 dependencies: platforms, clients, suppliers, landlords, employers.
Score Ownership and Dependency for each from 1 to 10.
Pick the worst ratio and name one thing you could own instead.
Start building that alternative now, before the dependency breaks.
Cut your reliance on it by a real, measurable amount this quarter.
equation_example: Ownership 8, Dependency 6. 8 ÷ 6 = 1.3. Above 1 means you've got more control than exposure. Below 1 means someone else is basically holding the steering wheel.
question: Name the one dependency that would hurt most if it disappeared tomorrow.
closing_statement: Own what you can't afford to lose.
caption:
Principle Nº 187: System Ownership

One algorithm change and half your sales disappear. That's not a business you control.

Real control comes from owning the things you can't afford to lose access to.

Your turn: Name the one dependency that would hurt most if it disappeared tomorrow.
